text:
priya: quick heads-up — during the 17:00-18:00 UTC shoulder we saw a sustained ~10% drop in global tokens/sec coming out of eu-west -> apac nodes. CPU on host fine, GPU util steady, but tail latency and token throughput dropped. anyone else seeing network saturation / PCIe stalls?

sam: saw same in the trace. egress to APAC spiked and packet retransmits increased. not pure GPU.

jeff: link stats? can you paste the curl to the debug endpoint?

priya: here's the sample we pulled from the probe: 
```
$ curl -s http://node-42.internal/debug/egress | jq '.ifstats | {tx_mbps, rx_mbps, errors, drops}'
{ "tx_mbps": 720, "rx_mbps": 680, "errors": 12, "drops": 5 }
```

oli: that tx is high for that rack — our NICs are 25G, but oversubscription + multiple colocated pods can push bursts. also saw increased `ksoftirq` on host.

capacity-bot: alert: apac-egress-rate-limit hit on cluster-redwood-apac-1 at 2026-03-18T17:23:04Z (:warning:)

priya: interesting — capacity implications: if network egress limits reduce tokens/sec by ~10% during shoulder, our throughput modeling should fold in network headroom, not just GPU hours. otherwise our GPU-hour forecasts will undercommit and latency SLOs break.

sam: agree. propose adding a network-contended scenario to the throughput simulator. quick patch idea: scale effective tps by min(gpu_capacity_factor, network_capacity_factor). network_capacity_factor = available_egress / baseline_egress.

jeff: +1. also add jittered short bursts for multi-tenant racks — worst-case 95th percentile matters for SLA.

priya: rough config we can use in sim (feel free to iterate):
```json
{
  "baseline_tokens_per_sec": 150000,
  "gpu_headroom_factor": 0.9,
  "network_capacity_factor": 0.88,
  "concurrent_requests": 1200,
  "burst_seconds": 45
}
```

oli: note: packing policy (fractional GPU slab) changes effective concurrency — when eviction happens we see latency cliffs. add a policy param `slab_fragmentation` to the model (0..1).

priya: action items: @sam will add the network_capacity_factor into the sim and run a 30d shoulder-run; @oli add slab_fragmentation sweep; @jeff produce new GPU-hour delta report comparing old sim vs contended sim. i'll open a follow-up thread with sim results.

sam: i'll start the sim tomorrow morning and post CSVs. tagging @robin for cost impact once we have deltas.

robin: FYI finance — if contended scenarios raise committed GPU-hours by >8% we need to re-evaluate reserved capacity buys for Q3.

priya: thanks all. small note: if we can route some APAC-bound inference to closer regional variants (even quantized ones) during short bursts, that might be cheaper than buying more reserve GPU hours. please include a reroute policy experiment in the sim. :mag_right:
